bug_semantics: isPrivateIP() in kernel/util/net.go is the IP allow/deny predicate behind SSRFSafeDialer, the SafeMode SSRF guard used by the network forward proxy (/api/network/forwardProxy), WebSocket proxy, and SSE proxy. The function checks only Go stdlib predicates — IsLoopback, IsLinkLocalUnicast, IsPrivate, IsUnspecified — which do NOT recognize IPv6 transition addresses embedding private IPv4: NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96), 6to4 (2002::/16), and Teredo (2001::/32). With SafeMode enabled, an authenticated attacker supplies a URL whose hostname resolves to such a transition address; the dialer's Control hook parses a global-looking IPv6 and permits the dial, and the kernel connects to the embedded private IPv4 — reaching internal services and cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) (CWE-918 SSRF).
flaw_origin: Commit dda0fb91367ad6c523a72e5dfd4ceb88c04a9699 ("Add Generic Streamed Proxy Responses for Kernel Plugins (#17748)", 2026-05-29, author mm-o <fly.x@outlook.com>, committer GitHub) moved the SSRF guard into kernel/util/net.go as the reusable SSRFSafeDialer and relocated the exact vulnerable predicate `func isPrivateIP(ip net.IP) bool { return ip.IsLoopback() || ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() || ip.IsPrivate() || ip.IsUnspecified() }` from kernel/api/network.go into the shared guard. The predicate itself was created by 3284e10028de39c8afc21b020498144714503fe1 (":lock: Fix" GHSA-56cv-c5p2-j2wg, 2026-03-11, Daniel) as the anti-SSRF/dns-rebinding dialer for forwardProxy; both commits encode the same incomplete stdlib-only classification. The advisory targets the isPrivateIP function in kernel/util/net.go used by SSRFSafeDialer — that function object first exists at dda0fb91 in net.go (parent 899b8c6e has no isPrivateIP/SSRFSafeDialer in kernel/util — introducer_parent_absent=true for the named sink), with 3284e100 as the originating design.

evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-74905 / GHSA-qrjw-gxw5-x7q9, upstream advisory GHSA-qq8m-8p8v-x4xg, VulnCheck): SiYuan before v3.7.4 — isPrivateIP in kernel/util/net.go used by SSRFSafeDialer misses IPv6 transition addresses (NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo 2001::/32) embedding private IPv4; authenticated attacker with SafeMode on reaches internal services and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) via network forward proxy / WebSocket proxy / SSE proxy; CWE-918.

BIC creation check: dda0fb91367a (2026-05-29) adds SSRFSafeDialer to kernel/util/net.go whose Control hook calls isPrivateIP with the stdlib-only body; the parent tree 899b8c6e has no isPrivateIP or SSRFSafeDialer in kernel/util (moved from kernel/api/network.go where 3284e10028de created it 2026-03-11 for GHSA-56cv-c5p2-j2wg).

Fix commit ecdf6038054d (2026-08-04, Daniel, GHSA-qq8m-8p8v-x4xg — the advisory's own reference): replaces the one-line predicate with loopback/link-local-unicast/link-local-multicast/private/unspecified/multicast checks PLUS explicit transition-address decoding — NAT64 (RFC 6052/8215 64:ff9b::/96 low-32), 6to4 (RFC 3056 2002::/16 bits 16-47), Teredo (RFC 4380 2001::/32 inverted low-32) — each recursing isPrivateIP on the embedded IPv4; +90 lines of net_test.go covering the transition forms. First tagged v3.8.0-alpha.1 → v3.8.0.

BIC version boundary: 3284e100 first tagged v3.6.0; dda0fb91 first tagged v3.7.0; the vulnerable shared guard shipped in v3.7.0–v3.7.3 (the advisory's 'before v3.7.4' window covers the named SSRFSafeDialer-in-net.go form; SafeMode itself was enabled by default in this range).

Sibling hardening in the same wave (distinct advisories, distinct paths): a8d2cc4e4952 (2026-08-10, GHSA-rg26-cg95-gq6p, CheckHostSSRF transition bypass), dd2778b70d02 (2026-08-13, GHSA-x8gv-g2g3-65fj, DNS rebinding in agent HTTP tools) — neither replaces the ecdf6038 net.go predicate fix.
